Black Shuck.alt: A huge black dog crossing a rain-soaked lane near a medieval Norfolk church
Black Shuck.caption: A visual interpretation of the East Anglian legend
Black Shuck.pullquote: To meet his gaze, tradition holds, is to be marked for death within the twelvemonth.
Black Shuck.editorial: We chose to open the East Anglian black-dog tradition with Black Shuck because the 1577 Bungay account is one of the earliest dated, place-specific sightings in English folklore — a rare case where a supernatural legend is pinned to a named church, a named storm and a surviving contemporary pamphlet. The scorch marks on the door of Holy Trinity, Blythburgh are still shown to visitors today.

Lambton Worm.alt: An enormous dark serpent coiling through the shallows of the River Wear
Lambton Worm.caption: A visual interpretation of the County Durham legend
Lambton Worm.pullquote: He must then slay the first living thing he met, or a curse would fall on nine generations of Lambtons.

Barghest.alt: A large black hound standing beside an old Yorkshire churchyard
Barghest.caption: A visual interpretation of the Yorkshire legend
Barghest.pullquote: To see the Barghest, or to hear its howl, was widely held to be an omen of death.

The Loch Ness Monster.alt: A long dark creature breaking the surface of Loch Ness beneath misty Highland slopes
The Loch Ness Monster.caption: A visual interpretation of the Loch Ness legend
The Loch Ness Monster.pullquote: Modern Nessie has been hunted by cameras, submarines and sonar for over a century, always elusive.

The Green Man.alt: A weathered Green Man carving with a leaf-framed face set into the stone of a medieval Gloucestershire church
The Green Man.caption: A visual interpretation of the Gloucestershire Green Man tradition
The Green Man.pullquote: Though Christian craftsmen cut him into the bosses and capitals of medieval churches, his roots seem far older.

Kelpie.alt: A black horse-like spirit standing chest-deep at the edge of a Highland loch under heavy clouds
Kelpie.caption: A visual interpretation of the Highland kelpie tradition
Kelpie.section_heading: The horse at the water's edge
Kelpie.pullquote: The moment a rider mounts they find themselves stuck fast as the creature plunges into the deep to drown and devour them.
